name: Khronon-Projected Finite-Norm Screened Preferred-Frame Constraint
claimed_mechanism: A nondynamical khronon A0 supplies an unremovable preferred-frame time direction that cannot be gauged away. A Lagrange multiplier constrains the chi propagation along A0, while the only e^{-y}-screened coupling is the A0-weighted preferred-frame force. The chi kinetic term is kept canonical and unscreened, so the propagating mode has a finite kinetic normalization independent of the screening factor. This separates the screened preferred-frame response from the finite kinetic norm and provides the A0 channel required for the lensing fix.
predicted_weak_field: In the low-acceleration regime the e^{-y} factor is unsuppressed, the constraint projects the scalar time derivative along A0, and the auxiliary chi realizes the MOND acceleration relation through mu(y). In the high-acceleration regime the screened A0 force is suppressed, the constraint reduces to a kinematic identity, and the canonical chi kinetic term remains finite without rescaling G. The unremovable A0 contribution to the metric sector gives the weak-field lensing ratio associated with the Bekenstein M5/M1=4 A0 structure.
inequivalence_argument: DC-001 is escaped because the candidate is no longer a local no-preferred-frame lensing MOND: it contains an unremovable khronon field A0 and every listed local coupling is preferred-frame, with the screened e^-y coupling supplying the required lensing escape. The finite propagating-mode norm is carried by the standard chi kinetic term and is not multiplied by e^-y, so the P7 collision is addressed by architecture rather than by tweaking a killed screened coefficient. The multiplier constraint projects chi dynamics along A0 instead of relying on a removable local vector or a nonlocal F+ functional. Therefore this is not a rename or coefficient variant of DC-001; the khronon sector and the separation of screened force from unscreened kinetic norm are new structural ingredients.
